title: an inferred-fallible callback reaching a consumer through an `as` cast must spell a Result contract
notes: specification/failures.mdx, 'Inference and Public Contracts': 'Public, abstract, ambient, and declaration-only contracts MUST express fallibility directly with `Result<A, E>` or `Promise<Result<A, E>>`.' A callback boundary is a VALUE edge, not an argument position: the callee invokes a function it received inside an object literal, an array literal, a parenthesis, a cast or a `new` argument list exactly as it invokes one passed directly. Fail-closed matters here because the accepting behaviour is silent and wrong rather than loud and wrong — R1FIX executed this class before the fix and measured `isOk() === true` with a `Result` sitting in the SUCCESS payload, with zero language diagnostics and zero emitted-TypeScript diagnostics. An `as` cast is the shape most likely to be mistaken for a contract: it states a type for the value the consumer receives, and it is exactly the spelling an author reaches for when the checker complains. It is not a Result contract, and asserting a plain function type over an inferred-fallible function is the assertion the rule exists to refuse. Charged at the arrow inside the cast.
